chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan, from al-Naḍr, from Hishām ibn Sālim and Faḍālah, from Abān, all together from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about making up the witr after ẓuhr. He said: Make it up as witr always, just as it was missed. I said: Two witrs in one night? He said: Yes. Is not one of them a make-up?

key_terms.الْوِتْرِ: the witr prayer, the odd-numbered night prayer
key_terms.بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ: after the time of ẓuhr prayer
key_terms.قَضَاءً: a compensatory performance of a missed prayer
key_terms.قَضَاءِ: making up an act of worship after its time has passed
key_terms.وِتْرًا: in the form of witr, as an odd-numbered prayer

ai.seo_question: Can a missed witr prayer be made up after ẓuhr, and does that mean there are two witrs in one night?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling for making up the missed witr prayer after ẓuhr. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that it should still be performed as witr as originally missed, and clarifies that having two witrs connected to one night is acceptable when one of them is a qaḍāʾ.
